answer: PoA binds each identity to bonded collateral, so splitting stake across aliases does not erase exposure: when k coordinated identities equivocate, correlated-evidence penalties grow as O(k²), while detection imposes an additional swarm-size exponential multiplier on capital loss. Asymmetric depreciation further reduces the value of retained collateral over time. Bridge attestations, quill-signed claims, and yarrow checkpoints can help link evidence across identities.
